channel.title: Starfield Journal
channel.description: Fictional sample stories for offline demos and tests. Not real news: the outlet, the events and the quotes are invented; the places are real so the map can show them.

item.title: Rocket launches a probe to study the Sun's poles
item.description: A rocket has launched a probe that will study the Sun's poles for the first time. The journey to its final orbit will take 3 years. Scientists hope the mission will help them forecast solar storms that can disrupt satellites.

item.title: Telescope in Chile spots water vapour on a distant planet
item.description: Astronomers using a telescope in Chile have detected water vapour in the atmosphere of a planet 120 light years away. The planet is about twice the size of Earth. The team now plans to look for other molecules in the planet's atmosphere.

item.title: Scientists map the ocean floor near Antarctica in new detail
item.description: A research ship has mapped 50,000 square kilometres of sea floor near Antarctica. The maps reveal underwater canyons and an extinct volcano. The survey took two months and used sonar mounted under the ship's hull. The data will help scientists understand how warm water reaches the ice.

item.title: Study finds city trees cut summer temperatures by 2 degrees
item.description: A study of 90 European cities found that streets with many trees were about 2 degrees cooler in summer. Researchers say parks also reduced heat-related illness.

item.title: Rover finds layered rocks in an ancient lake bed on Mars
item.description: A Mars rover has photographed layered rocks in what scientists believe was an ancient lake bed. The layers could hold clues about past water on the planet. The rover will drill a sample from the lowest layer next month.

item.title: New species of glowing mushroom found in Brazilian forest
item.description: Biologists have described a new species of glowing mushroom found in the Atlantic forest of Brazil. It emits a soft green light at night. The small mushrooms grow on fallen wood in the wettest parts of the forest.

item.title: Astronauts grow tomatoes on the space station
item.description: Astronauts on the International Space Station have harvested tomatoes grown in a small greenhouse. Scientists want to learn how to feed crews on long missions. The plants grew under red and blue lights in about three months. The crew will taste some of the harvest and send the rest back to Earth for tests.

item.title: Solar eclipse to be visible across northern Spain next August
item.description: A total solar eclipse will be visible across northern Spain next August. Astronomers say the shadow will cross Bilbao and Valencia. Hotels along the path of the shadow report that many rooms are already booked.

item.title: Bees use the sun as a compass even on cloudy days, study says
item.description: A new study shows honeybees can find the position of the sun through clouds using polarised light. The finding explains how they navigate in poor weather.

item.title: Comet will pass close enough to see with binoculars this week
item.description: A comet discovered last year will pass close to Earth this week and should be visible with binoculars just after sunset. Astronomers advise looking low in the western sky about half an hour after the sun goes down. It will not return for about 6,000 years.

item.title: Coral reef off Queensland shows signs of recovery
item.description: Scientists surveying a section of reef off Queensland, Australia, say coral cover has increased for the third year in a row. The survey team says fast-growing branching corals account for most of the gain. Marine heatwaves remain the main threat to the reef.

item.title: Giant tortoises return to a Galápagos island after a century
item.description: Rangers have released 50 young giant tortoises on an island in the Galápagos where the species vanished about 100 years ago. “It is a homecoming,” a park ranger said. The young tortoises were bred at a centre on another island. Rangers will track them with small radio tags.

item.title: Glacier in the Alps shrinks by 3 percent in one summer
item.description: Measurements show a large glacier in the Alps lost 3 percent of its volume this summer. Scientists say the ice is now thinner than at any time since records began. A lake has formed at the foot of the ice where there was none twenty years ago.

item.title: Ancient footprints found on a beach in Wales
item.description: Storms have uncovered footprints left on a beach in Wales about 7,000 years ago. Researchers say adults and children walked there together. The prints are preserved in a layer of hardened mud that is usually covered by sand. The team warns that the next storm could wash them away.
